From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options + pilot credits question

Hi Stella — thanks for the clear list. I put together the quick answers below and attached a pricing grid and a draft SOW for your procurement/legal team. TL;DR: we recommend starting on our Flex tier with a small Dedicated pool for prod; sandbox on hosted.

1) Recommended baseline (based on ~20k tokens/day):
   - Sandbox: Hosted API (free dev tier) — no commit needed.
   - Dev: Flex tier (metered) — low commit, supports autoscale; includes streaming and standard observability.
   - Prod: Small Dedicated pool (2 x A100 equivalent) with predictable throughput — reserved capacity for SLA.

2) Upgrade/downgrade path:
   - Upgrading: can scale Dedicated pools up in 24-48 hours; we can provision temporary burst capacity for the first two weeks to smooth traffic.
   - Downgrading: you can reduce committed capacity at the next billing cycle with a 30-day notice; there is a prorated credit for unused committed units.
   - Moving capacity between "environments": we support tagging and reassigning nodes; there is a short planning window (typically 72 hours) to migrate steady-state traffic.

3) Features vs add-ons:
   - Included in Flex/Hosted: streaming responses, standard tracing, model catalog access (open models).
   - Included in Dedicated: above plus prefix/KV caching, higher throughput kernels, SLA, and dedicated monitoring.
   - Add-ons: Private deployment (VPC/on-prem), extended retention for logs, KMS/HSM integration (enterprise).

4) Onboarding/pilot credits:
   - We can offer a 60% pilot credit applied to the first 90 days on Dedicated (applies to committed capacity for initial 3 months) + two free onboarding sessions with our solutions team.

Next steps: I've attached the redwood-pricing-grid.xlsx and a draft Medicore_SOW_draft.pdf to help procurement/legal. Ben — can you confirm the discount/credit structure and whether we need an MOU before DocuSign?

Happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow to walk the grid with the procurement team.

Best,
Vivek
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-pricing-grid.xlsx (pricing tiers and upgrade paths), Medicore_SOW_draft.pdf (SOW stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options + pilot credits question

Thanks Vivek — Stella, quick follow from my side on the commercials.

- Pilot discount: I can confirm the 60% credit on first 90 days for an initial Dedicated reservation up to $25k/mo committed. If Medicore wants a larger pilot, we can tier that to 75% on cards above $25k for the first month only.
- MOU vs SOW: procurement typically wants a simple MOU before full SOW/Order Form. We can provide a one-page MOU that outlines term, pilot credits, and expected timelines; SOW will follow and include implementation schedule.
- Downgrade credits: We offer prorated credits for reductions with a 30-day notice; if there is an early termination within initial 3-month pilot we will negotiate back credits case-by-case (we've done split refunds for pilot customers before).

Stella — if that works, Marissa will own onboarding and will schedule the enablement sessions; after MOU is signed we'll push the DocuSign order form and set up your Dedicated pool on a test NV (non-prod) cluster.

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
